audit_result.proof_trace: `handleConsent` reads `redirect_uri` from untrusted `formData` (L19) and validates `client_id` via DB RPC (L51) but never calls `isValidRedirectUri` or any equivalent check against the application's registered redirect URI allowlist. The `GET /oauth/authorize` route validates `redirect_uri` at L94, but this is a separate HTTP handler — it does not constrain what `redirect_uri` value the server action receives, and Next.js Server Actions can be invoked directly via POST without going through the consent UI.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An authenticated attacker POSTs directly to the `handleConsent` server action with a valid `client_id` and an arbitrary `redirect_uri=https://attacker.com/steal`; the handler issues a real authorization code and redirects to the attacker's URI (L106–109), enabling authorization code interception. Additionally, the `action=deny` path (L28–34) is an unauthenticated open redirect requiring no client_id validation at all.

PROP-stem-system-inv-004.text: Consent handler must re-validate client_id and redirect_uri server-side against DB, not trust formData.
PROP-stem-system-inv-004.assertion: forall consent: handle_consent(consent) => validate_client(consent.client_id) AND validate_uri(consent.redirect_uri)
